comments.note: resolveItemsPerPage() does not validate the value loaded from GridSettings against the configured $itemsPerPageOptions list. If the options list changes between sessions (e.g., 50 was once valid but is now removed), the stale stored value would be returned and no <option> would be rendered as selected in the selector, silently producing an inconsistent UI state. Consider validating the GridSettings value against the whitelist and falling through to $fallback if it no longer qualifies.

Bootstrap5Renderer::createItemsPerPageSelector() wraps the <select> in a flex div but does not add an aria-label to the <select> or a visible <label> element. Screen readers have no announcement for the control's purpose. Adding aria-label="Items per page" to the <select> tag would satisfy WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.1 with minimal effort.

The early-return guard (totalPages <= 1 && !hasItemsPerPageOptions()) is duplicated verbatim in both BaseGridRenderer::renderPaginationRow() and Bootstrap5Renderer::renderPaginationRow(). This is unavoidable given the full override architecture but is worth flagging for a future refactor — e.g., extracting the guard into a protected shouldRenderPaginationRow() helper on the base class.

The ?? $fallback null guard in resolveItemsPerPage() after GridSettings::getItemsPerPage($fallback) is technically redundant: when a non-null $fallback is passed, getItemsPerPage() cannot return null. However, the guard is correct given the ?int return type annotation and acts as defensive code. No action required; noting for clarity.
